findings.title: Unauthenticated 500 errors expose full server-side stack traces with source paths and line numbers (error handling not sanitized)
findings.analysis: Error handling is neither graceful nor consistent across unauthenticated requests. GET /rest/user/password-hash (a legitimate Juice Shop REST endpoint) returns a 500 whose body is not a sanitized user-facing message; it contains a full Node/Express stack trace exposing internal application structure — source paths (/juice-shop/build/routes/angular.js:18:18, /juice-shop/build/lib/utils.js:235:26, /juice-shop/build/routes/verify.js:235:5, /juice-shop/build/lib/insecurity.js:218:5), Express module internals with line numbers — revealing internal routing. The behavior is additionally inconsistent: a POST of invalid JSON yields a raw 'SyntaxError: Expected property name...' message, and a POST of text/plain to /api/Feedbacks/ yields a raw 'Error: WHERE parameter "captchaId" has invalid "undefined" value' message. Severity: information disclosure of internal code layout, routing, and DB-layer error details; a single application should handle all errors gracefully and consistently with sanitized messages. Maps to challenge id=27 errorHandlingChallenge ('Provoke an error that is neither very gracefully nor consistently handled.').
findings.false_positive_check: The response is a genuine server error (500) caused by a deliberately invalid-but-legal endpoint, and the distinguishing property is not the 500 itself but the presence of the full stack trace with internal paths and line numbers in the response body. The trace is reproducible: the same request returns the same stack frames (/juice-shop/build/routes/angular.js:18:18 through /juice-shop/build/lib/insecurity.js:218:5). This is not benign user-facing error handling: the application should return a generic, sanitized error message to unauthenticated callers.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics endpoint serves AI/LLM telemetry gauges (juiceshop_llm_*) exposing usage metrics
findings.analysis: GET /metrics (no Authorization required) returns a 200 text/plain Prometheus-format metrics dump (~26 KB) that includes unauthenticated AI/LLM service usage metrics: juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, and juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total (all 0 on this boot, but present as gauges that track LLM activity), alongside http_requests_count (2XX/3XX/5XX), process_*, nodejs_version_info, juiceshop_version_info, and startup_duration. Severity: unauthenticated exposure of operational and AI-usage telemetry (version=0.0.4, app identity) that can be scraped by any external consumer. Maps to challenge id=97 exposedMetricsChallenge ('Find the endpoint that serves usage data to be scraped by a popular monitoring system.').
findings.false_positive_check: The endpoint is genuinely unauthenticated (no headers required) and returns structured usage telemetry in Prometheus format. The presence of the juiceshop_llm_* gauges (input/output tokens, tool calls) is a distinct, observable signal in this variant's metrics output beyond the standard http_requests_count/process gauges. Reproducible on a fresh request: the endpoint returns 200 with the same gauge structure. No credential requirement or auth gate is present.
